case_name: Jagdeep Kaur And Anr v. State Of Punjab And Ors

parties.respondent_defendant: State of Punjab and others (government agency)

facts_of_case: Petitioners are a couple who got married despite parents' opposition. They claim threats from private respondents to break their marriage.

legal_principles.principle: The essential condition of Hindu Marriage Act is that the bridegroom must be above 21 years and the bride above 18 years.
legal_principles.held: A perusal of Section 5, ibid leaves no manner of doubt that one of the essential conditions of Hindu Marriage Act is that the bridegroom must be above 21 years and the bride above 18 years.

legal_principles.principle: A marriage solemnized in contravention of Sub Section (iii) of Section 5 is not void or invalid.
legal_principles.held: However, at the same time, Section 11 of the Hindu Marriage Act which declares certain marriages, which are in contravention of Section 5 (supra), to be void, but precludes a marriage solemnized in contravention of Sub Section (iii) of Section 5 from the purview of being regarded as void or invalid.
cited_cases: Jitender Kumar Sharma Vs. State and Another, (2001) 7 AD (Delhi) 785

outcome.final_order: Appropriate protection granted to petitioners for their life and liberty as apprehended by them.

use_for_drafting: advising on minor marriage consent issues
